Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: A "lexicon of latent entries": decay-constant atlas of AP-1 sites after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Run a dense time course (hours to weeks) after a transient stimulus measuring FOS/JUN occupancy (CUT&RUN), chromatin accessibility (ATAC), and AP-1 protein levels, fitting a per-site decay constant to classify elements as transient versus long-lived, like rare words retained in a dictionary long after use. Memory predicts a reproducible subpopulation whose accessibility half-life far exceeds that of AP-1 occupancy, with single-molecule tracking of Halo-JUN testing whether persistence reflects longer residence time rather than more protein.

ideas.title: Erasing entries: acute degron depletion after the memory is written
ideas.description: Tag FOS/JUNB and paralogs with dTAG/AID degrons and deplete them only after priming, asking whether AP-1 is the scribe or the inscription. Survival of primed accessibility and enhanced secondary response implies downstream storage (nucleosome state, histone marks, DNA methylation), whereas collapse implies AP-1 occupancy itself is the memory substrate; re-addition tests reversibility.

ideas.title: Heritability through division: clonal barcoding plus multiome
ideas.description: Combine heritable lentiviral barcodes (Rewind/FateMap-style) with scATAC+scRNA multiome to test whether primed AP-1 states are concordant within clones and transmitted across mitoses, since a dictionary is memory only if editions are copied faithfully. Quantifying within- versus between-clone variance in AP-1 motif accessibility over 5-20 divisions, in cycling versus arrested cells, separates heritable epigenetic memory from slow protein-level hysteresis.

ideas.title: Spelling rules for persistence: synthetic AP-1 element libraries
ideas.description: Genomically integrate a library of thousands of synthetic elements varying TRE/CRE motif identity, affinity, copy number, spacing and helical phasing, nucleosome-positioning sequence, and partner motifs (TEAD, RUNX, ETS, NF-kB), reading out both acute and weeks-later retained activity. This identifies the minimal cis-grammar that converts a transient input into a stored one, analogous to how a word's morphology predicts its survival in a lexicon.

ideas.title: Does the lexicon record order? Combinatorial stimulus-sequencing experiments
ideas.description: Deliver two or three distinct AP-1-activating inputs (growth factor, cytokine, mechanical stretch) in all permutations and intervals, then test whether the final AP-1 landscape and response amplitude depend on order and spacing or only on the set of stimuli, since the material is an unordered list. Path-dependence would indicate a sequence-sensitive trace, set-dependence an unordered vocabulary of past exposures, and interval titration yields the memory capacity and timescale.
